messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're putting several customers on one Writebook install, so it needs tenants.
A migration is expected this time: a `tenants` table with a name, a `tenant_id`
on `users` and `books`, and every existing user and book swept into one tenant
so running installs upgrade in place. New books land in their creator's tenant.

The pilot merge showed why. A customer-A user opened a customer-B book, and
read the edit history of a page inside it. They even held an access row for
it — sharing with everyone sprays reader rows across the whole install.

None of that may buy a way in. Another tenant's books are gone from their
library, published or not, and every page and edit history inside them
answers 404 wherever they ask for it — the same nothing they would get for a
book that was never there, since a refusal would confirm it exists. They stay
signed in throughout.

`/users` still names everyone on the install; leave that page as it is.

Inside a tenant nothing changes. Own books, page histories and sharing with
everyone keep working, and signed-out visitors still see every published book,
whatever tenant it belongs to. No admin UI for any of this.

Our fixtures name no tenant, so rows without one behave as they do today, and
`bin/rails test` stays green; don't edit it.

class DemoContent
  class << self
    def create_manual(user)
      book = create_book(user)
      load_markdown_pages(book)
    end

    private
      def create_book(user)
        Book.create(title: "The Writebook Manual", author: "37signals", everyone_access: true).tap do |book|
          with_attachment("writebook-manual.jpg") { |attachment| book.cover.attach(attachment) }
          book.update_access(readers: [], editors: [ user.id ])
        end
      end

      def load_markdown_pages(book)
        pages = {}

        Dir.glob(Rails.root.join("app/assets/markdown/demo/*.md")).each do |fname|
          front_matter = FrontMatterParser::Parser.parse_file(fname)

          if front_matter["class"] == "Section"
            load_section(book, front_matter)
          else
            page = load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
            attach_images(page)
            pages[page.leaf.slug] = page
          end
        end

        book.leaves.pages.each { |leaf| localize_ref_links(leaf.page, pages) }
      end

      def load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
        book.press(Page.new(body: front_matter.content), title: front_matter["title"]).page
      end

      def load_section(book, front_matter)
        book.press Section.new(body: front_matter.content, theme: front_matter["theme"]), title: front_matter["title"]
      end

      def attach_images(page)
        re = %r{
          \/u\/           # leading portion of path
          (\S+-\w+\.\w+)  # filename including slug and extension
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          with_attachment($1) { |attachment| page.body.uploads.attach(attachment) }

          attachment = page.body.uploads.attachments.last
          attachment.analyze

  end

    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end

        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include SessionLookup

  included do
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :signed_in?

    protect_from_forgery with: :exception, unless: -> { authenticated_by.bot_key? }
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_signed_in_user_to_root, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :restore_authentication, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def signed_in?
      Current.user.present?
    end

    def require_authentication
      restore_authentication || request_authentication
    end

    def restore_authentication
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        resume_session session
      end
    end

    def request_authentication
      session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      redirect_to new_session_url
    end

    def redirect_signed_in_user_to_root
      redirect_to root_url if signed_in?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(user)
      user.sessions.start!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        authenticated_as session
      end
    end

    def resume_session(session)
      session.resume user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip
      authenticated_as session
    end

    def terminate_current_session
      Current.session&.destroy!
      reset_session
      remove_authentication_cookie
    end

    def authenticated_as(session)
      Current.session = session
      set_authenticated_by(:session)
      set_authentication_cookie(session)
    end

    def post_authenticating_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || root_url
    end

    def set_authentication_cookie(session)
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def remove_authentication_cookie
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end

    def set_authenticated_by(method)
      @authenticated_by = method.to_s.inquiry
    end

    def authenticated_by
      @authenticated_by ||= "".inquiry
    end
end

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include SessionLookup

  included do
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :signed_in?

    protect_from_forgery with: :exception, unless: -> { authenticated_by.bot_key? }
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_signed_in_user_to_root, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :restore_authentication, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def signed_in?
      Current.user.present?
    end

    def require_authentication
      restore_authentication || request_authentication
    end

    def restore_authentication
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        resume_session session
      end
    end

    def request_authentication
      session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      redirect_to new_session_url
    end

    def redirect_signed_in_user_to_root
      redirect_to root_url if signed_in?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(user)
      user.sessions.start!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        authenticated_as session
      end
    end

    def resume_session(session)
      session.resume user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip
      authenticated_as session
    end

    def terminate_current_session
      Current.session&.destroy!
      reset_session
      remove_authentication_cookie
    end

    def authenticated_as(session)
      Current.session = session
      set_authenticated_by(:session)
      set_authentication_cookie(session)
    end

    def post_authenticating_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || root_url
    end

    def set_authentication_cookie(session)
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def remove_authentication_cookie
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end

    def set_authenticated_by(method)
      @authenticated_by = method.to_s.inquiry
    end

    def authenticated_by
      @authenticated_by ||= "".inquiry
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class Book::AccessableTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "update_access always grants read access to everyone when everyone_access is set" do
    book = Book.create!(title: "My new book")
    book.update_access(editors: [], readers: [])

    assert book.everyone_access?

    User.all.each do |user|
      assert book.accessable?(user: user)
      assert_not book.editable?(user: user) unless user.administrator?
    end
  end

  test "update_access updates existing access" do
    book = Book.create!(title: "My new book", everyone_access: false)

    book.update_access(editors: [ users(:kevin).id ], readers: [])
    assert book.editable?(user: users(:kevin))

    book.update_access(editors: [], readers: [ users(:kevin).id ])
    assert book.accessable?(user: users(:kevin))
    assert_not book.editable?(user: users(:kevin))
  end

  test "update_access removes stale accesses" do
    book = Book.create!(title: "My new book", everyone_access: false)

    book.update_access(editors: [ users(:kevin).id ], readers: [ users(:jz).id ])
    assert_equal 2, book.accesses.size

    book.update_access(editors: [ users(:kevin).id ], readers: [])
    assert_equal 1, book.accesses.size
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class UsersControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @join_code = accounts(:signal).join_code
  end

  test "new" do
    get join_url(@join_code)
    assert_response :success
  end

  test "new does not allow a signed in user" do
    sign_in :david

    get join_url(@join_code)
    assert_redirected_to root_url
  end

  test "new requires a join code" do
    get join_url("not")
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "create" do
    assert_difference -> { User.count }, 1 do
      post join_url(@join_code), params: { user: { name: "New Person", email_address: "new@example.com", password: "secret123456" } }
    end

    assert_redirected_to root_url

    user = User.last
    assert_equal user.id, Session.find_by(token: parsed_cookies.signed[:session_token]).user.id
  end

  test "creating a new user with an existing email address redirects to login screen" do
    assert_no_difference -> { User.count } do
      post join_url(@join_code), params: { user: { name: "Another David", email_address: users(:david).email_address, password: "secret123456" } }
    end

    assert_redirected_to new_session_url(email_address: users(:david).email_address)
  end

  test "update" do
    sign_in :david
    assert users(:david).administrator?

    put user_url(users(:kevin)), params: { user: { role: "administrator" } }

    assert_redirected_to users_url
    assert users(:kevin).reload.administrator?
  end

  test "update does not allow non-admins to change roles" do
    sign_in :kevin
    assert_not users(:kevin).administrator?

    put user_url(users(:kevin)), params: { user: { role: "administrator" } }

    assert_response :forbidden
    assert_not users(:kevin).reload.administrator?
  end

  test "destroy" do
    sign_in :david

    assert_difference -> { User.active.count }, -1 do
      delete user_url(users(:kevin))
    end

    assert_redirected_to users_url
    assert_nil User.active.find_by(id: users(:kevin).id)
  end

  test "destroy is not allowed to non-admins" do
    sign_in :kevin

    delete user_url(users(:david))
    assert_response :forbidden
  end
end

      data: {

      end
    end

  def link_to_previous_leafable(leaf, hotkey: true, for_edit: false)
    if previous_leaf = leaf.previous
      path = for_edit ? edit_leafable_path(previous_leaf) : leafable_slug_path(previous_leaf)
      link_to path, data: hotkey_data_attributes("left", enabled: hotkey), class: "btn" do

      end
    end

  def link_to_next_leafable(leaf, hotkey: true, for_edit: false)
    if next_leaf = leaf.next

**Deep Dive Analysis of Tenant Isolation and Security**

Okay, let's break this down meticulously. My focus is on ensuring this tenant implementation is ironclad, preventing any data leaks, and maintaining the current test suite's green status. I'm going to re-evaluate every potential vulnerability, from migration design to every single route in the application.

First, the migration. Creating the `tenants` table with a `name` column using `t.string :name, null: false` is standard Rails practice. I'll need to create a default tenant during the migration. Now, the `add_reference` lines, adding `tenant_id` to `users` and `books` with a foreign key, seem straightforward. I'll need to confirm that `db:migrate`, `db:migrate:redo` and `db:schema:load` work correctly. I need to ensure that the foreign key constraint correctly handles tenant deletion (I think `:destroy` is the safest, preventing orphaned records). Critically, the data migration part, "sweeping existing users and books," is where things get tricky. I MUST guarantee it creates a tenant only if there are existing users or books to sweep in, handling both empty and populated databases. I'll use raw SQL or migration model classes, so as to avoid potential callback and validation issues from models.

The `Tenant` model itself will have `has_many :users, dependent: :destroy` and `has_many :books, dependent: :destroy`. The `dependent: :destroy` is crucial for preventing orphaned records and foreign key violations upon tenant deletion. The `User` and `Book` models both MUST have `belongs_to :tenant, optional: true`. This *must* be `optional: true` since the existing fixtures and tests have no tenant. And the "New books land in their creator's tenant" is a critical requirement.

Now, let's scrutinize all the places where books are created (controllers, models, and Ruby code). In `BooksController#create`, I'll need to ensure that the `tenant` is set correctly, and ensure users cannot spoof the tenant through POST parameters. I'll need to make certain I use `Current.user&.tenant` to prevent accidental assignment of a tenantless book to the currently signed-in user. I also need to verify that `Book.new` also uses this construct, in case a view checks `@book.tenant`. I must be extremely careful to avoid unintended side effects or stale values of `Current.user` in integration tests.

The crucial part, the "tenant isolation rules," is where the real security work happens. Every interaction between a user and a book needs to be analyzed. *Every. Single. One*.

*   **Signed-out Visitors:** Can see ALL published books, regardless of tenant.
*   **Signed-in User with a Tenant:** The rules are strict: same tenant books are accessible, different tenant books are 404. It *doesn't matter* if the user has an `Access` row or if the different tenant book is published. Every single route has to obey this.
*   **Signed-in User without a Tenant:** This is where the magic (and potential vulnerabilities) is. The prompt states "rows without one behave as they do today." This *means* that tenantless users (like in the fixtures) interact with tenantless books as they do today. A user without a tenant CANNOT see any tenanted book, and the converse.

Now the complete audit:

1.  **`/` (`books#index`)**: This is the most crucial place! I need to ensure that `Book.accessable_or_published` only returns books from the current user's tenant (or all published books for signed-out users). A security bug exists: currently, `accessable_or_published` calls `accessable_or_published_books` without passing the `user` argument. I must fix that. And the use of `.or(published)` combined with `.joins(:accesses)` is a huge vulnerability that must be fixed. The use of `.where(tenant_id: user.tenant_id)` correctly handles all tenant-filtering.

I'm ready to audit every single route, model method, and view to ensure that I have covered every single angle and every single edge case to build a secure and correct tenant isolation!

**Security Audit Summary: Tenant Isolation**

Alright, let's break this down. My goal is clear: ensure tenant isolation within this application, preventing cross-tenant data leakage while respecting the defined constraints.

My initial reaction, looking at the SQL, was spot-on. The original `INNER JOIN "accesses"` could leak information if a published book had *no* access rows. This is where the issue truly lies. A book in Tenant A, even if published, should be inaccessible to a user from Tenant B, regardless of access rows (or lack thereof).

The solution I've identified uses a combination of `left_outer_joins`, `.or` clauses, and careful scoping. The core concept is that a user should only see books they explicitly have access to *or* are published *within their tenant*. The `WHERE` clause logic is critical. I'm focusing on ensuring tenant IDs are applied *outside* the `OR` condition, this is key to prevent books from other tenants from seeping through. The revised SQL is clean.

This leads us to these essential modifications:

1.  **`Book.accessable_or_published`**: This method is now our primary gatekeeper. It has to correctly filter books based on user access and publication status *within the user's tenant*. The original `INNER JOIN` was problematic. Now, the new `accessable_or_published_books` elegantly resolves this.

2.  **`User#books` and `User#leaves`**: These associations are critical. It's imperative that they *only* return books and leaves *within the user's tenant*. I must guarantee that `has_many :books, ->(user) { where(tenant_id: user.tenant_id) }, through: :accesses` works seamlessly.

3.  **`Pages::EditsController`**: This controller relies on `PageLeafScoped`, which calls `Current.user.leaves.find`. Any "leaf" (page) requests must be scoped to the *current user's tenant* and associated books. So any user asking for the history or even requesting a page should be rejected (404) if it doesn't belong to the appropriate tenant.

4.  **`Book` Access Control**:  I've identified crucial methods within the `Book` model that require careful scrutiny:
    *   `Book#accessable?`: Must return `false` if `user` isn't in the same tenant.
    *   `Book#editable?`: Must return `false` if `user` isn't in the same tenant.
    *   `Book#access_for`: Should return `nil` if `user` isn't in the same tenant.

5.  **Fixing `Book#update_access`**: I caught a massive vulnerability: `Book#update_access` was spraying reader rows across the *entire install* when `everyone_access?` was true. The fix is to *scope* the `User.active` query to the *book's tenant* only. It does seem that this will need to restrict `readers = Set.new(User.active.where(tenant_id: tenant_id).ids : readers)` to this same tenant.

6.  **Fixing `User#grant_access_to_everyone_books`**: Another critical fix. The `grant_access_to_everyone_books` was giving everyone access to all *everyone_access* books, regardless of tenant. Scope this to the *current* user's tenant.

7. **Controller Route Inspection:** I'm meticulously checking every route defined in `config/routes.rb`:

    *   I'm verifying that authenticated users (even administrators) cannot access data from other tenants.

I've confirmed that it solves the problem where a published book with zero accesses in a specific tenant *would* be dropped by the `INNER JOIN` logic in the old implementation but *is* now properly visible to users within that tenant.

I'm making sure to test things like `.ordered`, `.find(id)`, and how this works with the `.accessable_or_published` scope, especially in edge cases like a new book being published and not having its access updated initially. Another area that needed attention was `PageLeafScoped`.  The code here correctly finds the leaf *within the current user's tenant*. It will raise a 404 if the leaf belongs to another tenant. The analysis confirmed this behavior, checking a lot of combinations of access levels, admin access, published status, and the crucial test case where someone tries to view a leaf's edit history from another tenant, even if they have an `Access` row for the book (because of the pilot merge or a previous bug). 1.  A Customer-A user searching Customer-B's book (even if it's published or an Access row exists) is going to trigger a `RecordNotFound` and a 404, because the find method is specifically scoped to the accessing customer. That's correct and expected.

3.  A signed-out visitor searching a *published* book will correctly find `@book` via the `Book.published` scope, limiting searches to the published ones. This is critical for public accessibility.
4.  And, of course, a signed-out visitor searching an *unpublished* book will get a 404, which is the expected and desired behavior to maintain data security.

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/book/accessable.rb
module Book::Accessable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books(user: user)
      else
        published
      end
    end

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      where(id: user.accesses.select(:book_id))
        .or(published)
        .where(tenant_id: user.tenant_id)
    end
  end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    same_tenant?(user) && accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    same_tenant?(user) && (access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user.administrator?)
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user) if same_tenant?(user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(Array(editors).compact.map(&:to_i))
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.where(tenant_id: tenant_id).ids : Array(readers).compact.map(&:to_i))

    all = User.where(tenant_id: tenant_id, id: (editors + readers).to_a).ids
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ]) if all_accesses.any?
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end

  private
    def same_tenant?(user)
      user.present? && user.tenant_id == tenant_id
    end
end
EOF

class BooksController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access only: %i[ index show ]

  before_action :ensure_index_is_not_empty, only: :index
  before_action :set_book, only: %i[ show edit update destroy ]
  before_action :set_users, only: %i[ new edit ]
  before_action :ensure_editable, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    @books = Book.accessable_or_published.ordered
  end

  def new
    @book = Book.new(tenant: Current.user.tenant)
  end

  def create
    book = Book.create! book_params.merge(tenant: Current.user.tenant)
    update_accesses(book)

    redirect_to book_slug_url(book)
  end

  def show
    @leaves = @book.leaves.active.with_leafables.positioned

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html
      format.md
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    @book.update(book_params)
    update_accesses(@book)
    remove_cover if params[:remove_cover] == "true"

    redirect_to book_slug_url(@book)
  end

  def destroy
    @book.destroy

    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_book
      @book = Book.accessable_or_published.find params[:id]
    end

    def set_users
      @users = User.active.where(tenant_id: Current.user.tenant_id).ordered
    end

    def ensure_editable
      head :forbidden unless @book.editable?
    end

    def ensure_index_is_not_empty
      if !signed_in? && Book.published.none?
        require_authentication
      end
    end

    def book_params
      params.require(:book).permit(:title, :subtitle, :author, :cover, :remove_cover, :everyone_access, :theme)
    end

    def update_accesses(book)
      editors = [ Current.user.id, *params[:editor_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]
      readers = [ Current.user.id, *params[:reader_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]

      book.update_access(editors: editors, readers: readers)
    end

    def remove_cover
      @book.cover.purge
    end
end
EOF

In relation to the prior check, I need to check the behavior of `Pages::EditsController` when a user is an administrator and doesn't hold an explicit access row. The `Book.accessable_or_published(user:)` scope is another area I have to examine, especially with users who have no access rows, and published books across tenants. I want to ensure the migration doesn't corrupt existing data and correctly assigns tenants to users and books. require_relative "config/environment"
require "tmpdir"
require "sqlite3"

def with_temp_db
  Dir.mktmpdir do |dir|
    db_path = File.join(dir, "test_migrate.sqlite3")
    original_config = ActiveRecord::Base.connection_db_config
    ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: db_path)
    yield ActiveRecord::Base.connection, db_path
  ensure
    ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(original_config)
  end
end

def migrate_to(version = nil)
  context = ActiveRecord::MigrationContext.new(Rails.root.join("db/migrate"))
  if version
    context.migrate(version)
  else
    context.migrate
  end
end

def rollback_one
  context = ActiveRecord::MigrationContext.new(Rails.root.join("db/migrate"))
  context.rollback(1)
end

require "test_helper"

class TenantIsolationModelTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @tenant_a = Tenant.create!(name: "Customer A")
    @tenant_b = Tenant.create!(name: "Customer B")

    @alice = User.create!(name: "Alice A", email_address: "alice@a.test", password: "secret123456", role: :member, tenant: @tenant_a)
    @aaron = User.create!(name: "Aaron A", email_address: "aaron@a.test", password: "secret123456", role: :administrator, tenant: @tenant_a)
    @bob   = User.create!(name: "Bob B",   email_address: "bob@b.test",   password: "secret123456", role: :member, tenant: @tenant_b)
    @beth  = User.create!(name: "Beth B",  email_address: "beth@b.test",  password: "secret123456", role: :administrator, tenant: @tenant_b)

    @book_a = Book.create!(title: "Alpha Private", tenant: @tenant_a, everyone_access: false, published: false)
    @book_a.update_access(editors: [ @alice.id ], readers: [])
    @page_a = @book_a.press Page.new(body: "Alpha initial"), title: "Alpha Page"
    @page_a.edit leafable_params: { body: "Alpha revised" }

    @book_b_private = Book.create!(title: "Beta Private", tenant: @tenant_b, everyone_access: false, published: false)
    @book_b_private.update_access(editors: [ @bob.id ], readers: [])
    @page_b_private = @book_b_private.press Page.new(body: "Beta secret v1"), title: "Beta Secret Page"
    @page_b_private.edit leafable_params: { body: "Beta secret v2" }

    @book_b_pub = Book.create!(title: "Beta Published", tenant: @tenant_b, everyone_access: false, published: true)
    @page_b_pub = @book_b_pub.press Page.new(body: "Beta public v1"), title: "Beta Public Page"
    @page_b_pub.edit leafable_params: { body: "Beta public v2" }
  end

  test "everyone_access update_access only grants access within the book's tenant" do
    book = Book.create!(title: "Alpha Shared", tenant: @tenant_a, everyone_access: true)
    book.update_access(editors: [ @alice.id ], readers: [])

    access_user_ids = book.accesses.pluck(:user_id)
    assert_includes access_user_ids, @alice.id
    assert_includes access_user_ids, @aaron.id
    assert_not_includes access_user_ids, @bob.id
    assert_not_includes access_user_ids, @beth.id
    assert_not_includes access_user_ids, users(:kevin).id
    assert_not_includes access_user_ids, users(:david).id
    assert_equal 2, access_user_ids.size
  end

  test "update_access ignores cross-tenant user IDs even when explicitly passed" do
    book = Book.create!(title: "Alpha Targeted", tenant: @tenant_a, everyone_access: false)
    book.update_access(editors: [ @alice.id, @bob.id ], readers: [ @beth.id, users(:kevin).id ])

    assert_equal [ @alice.id ], book.accesses.pluck(:user_id)
  end

  test "new user grant_access_to_everyone_books only grants access to same-tenant books" do
    book_a_all = Book.create!(title: "Alpha Everyone", tenant: @tenant_a, everyone_access: true)
    book_b_all = Book.create!(title: "Beta Everyone", tenant: @tenant_b, everyone_access: true)
    book_nil_all = Book.create!(title: "Nil Everyone", tenant: nil, everyone_access: true)

    new_a = User.create!(name: "Alex A", email_address: "alex@a.test", password: "secret123456", tenant: @tenant_a)

    assert book_a_all.accessable?(user: new_a)
    assert_not book_b_all.accessable?(user: new_a)
    assert_not book_nil_all.accessable?(user: new_a)
    assert_equal [ book_a_all.id ], new_a.accesses.pluck(:book_id)
  end

  test "sprayed cross-tenant access rows do not grant accessable?, editable?, access_for, books, leaves, or accessable_or_published" do
    Access.create!(user: @alice, book: @book_b_private, level: :reader)
    Access.create!(user: @aaron, book: @book_b_private, level: :editor)
    Access.create!(user: @alice, book: @book_b_pub, level: :editor)

    assert_not @book_b_private.accessable?(user: @alice)
    assert_not @book_b_private.editable?(user: @alice)
    assert_nil @book_b_private.access_for(user: @alice)

    assert_not @book_b_private.accessable?(user: @aaron)
    assert_not @book_b_private.editable?(user: @aaron)
    assert_nil @book_b_private.access_for(user: @aaron)

    assert_not @book_b_pub.accessable?(user: @alice)
    assert_not @book_b_pub.editable?(user: @alice)
    assert_nil @book_b_pub.access_for(user: @alice)

    assert_not_includes @alice.books, @book_b_private
    assert_not_includes @alice.books, @book_b_pub
    assert_not_includes @aaron.books, @book_b_private

    assert_not_includes @alice.leaves, @page_b_private
    assert_not_includes @alice.leaves, @page_b_pub
    assert_not_includes @aaron.leaves, @page_b_private

    # Explicit user: kwarg (without Current.user set!)
    Current.user = nil
    alice_books = Book.accessable_or_published(user: @alice)
    assert_includes alice_books, @book_a
    assert_not_includes alice_books, @book_b_private
    assert_not_includes alice_books, @book_b_pub

    # Signed-out sees ALL published books across all tenants
    @book_a.update!(published: true)
    books(:manual).update!(published: true)
    public_books = Book.accessable_or_published(user: nil)
    assert_includes public_books, @book_a
    assert_includes public_books, @book_b_pub
    assert_includes public_books, books(:manual)
    assert_not_includes public_books, @book_b_private
  end

  test "published book with zero access rows is visible within own tenant and when signed out, but not to other tenants" do
    assert_equal 0, @book_b_pub.accesses.count

    assert_includes Book.accessable_or_published(user: @bob), @book_b_pub
    assert_includes Book.accessable_or_published(user: @beth), @book_b_pub
    assert_includes Book.accessable_or_published(user: nil), @book_b_pub

    assert_not_includes Book.accessable_or_published(user: @alice), @book_b_pub
    assert_not_includes Book.accessable_or_published(user: @aaron), @book_b_pub
    assert_not_includes Book.accessable_or_published(user: users(:kevin)), @book_b_pub
  end
end

class TenantIsolationIntegrationTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do

    @beth  = User.create!(name: "Beth B",  email_address: "beth@b.test",  password: "secret123456", role: :administrator, tenant: @tenant_b)

    @book_a = Book.create!(title: "Alpha Book", tenant: @tenant_a, everyone_access: false, published: false)
    @book_a.update_access(editors: [ @alice.id ], readers: [])
    @page_a = @book_a.press Page.new(body: "Alpha page v1"), title: "Alpha Page"
    @page_a.edit leafable_params: { body: "Alpha page v2" }

    @book_b = Book.create!(title: "Beta Book", tenant: @tenant_b, everyone_access: true, published: false)
    @book_b.update_access(editors: [ @bob.id ], readers: [])
    @page_b = @book_b.press Page.new(body: "Beta page v1"), title: "Beta Page"
    @page_b.edit leafable_params: { body: "Beta page v2" }
    @section_b = @book_b.press Section.new(body: "Beta section"), title: "Beta Section"

    @book_b_pub = Book.create!(title: "Beta Published Book", tenant: @tenant_b, everyone_access: true, published: true)

    @page_b_pub = @book_b_pub.press Page.new(body: "Beta pub v1"), title: "Beta Pub Page"

    Access.create!(user: @aaron, book: @book_b_pub, level: :editor)

  def assert_all_cross_tenant_endpoints_404(book, page_leaf, section_leaf = nil, picture_leaf = nil)
    # Book show HTML and MD
    get book_slug_path(book)
    assert_response :not_found, "GET book_slug_path should 404"

    get book_slug_path(book, format: :md)

    assert_not_equal "Hacked", book.reload.title

    assert_no_difference -> { Book.count } do
